items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1961-01-29
items.q: And the rhythm section was, uh, let's see, we had, um, our shoulder blanching, and, um, let's see what we had on there, Ransom Island on bass, and, uh, a little fella named Bucket. He came here from Chicago. He stayed around here quite a while, and me on, I think I was playing banjo and, and straigh

ctx.x: And when did you go after this band broke up?

Well, as I said, we, we, in Pensacola, we were working for these people, and so, uh, we used to play a town like, like Mobile, and go to Montgomery, and, uh, there's a couple other times we'd go. So, uh, around about, uh, let's see, close to 26, well, we left Pensacola, no, we made a trip down to Florida, that's what we made, a trip all over from Pensacola to, uh, Jacksonville, Florida. Well, this guy, here in the...

he was managing the band and booking the band because they didn't have no bookies no day, but he was a man that knew a lot of people, you see. And we booked this all the way to Jacksonville. We stayed, I remember it was in the winter we were in Jacksonville, Florida. And the fella George Morris, he had been a cook one time. He suggested that we go down to Miami or Panama, way down up in there, you see. And well, the fella, they wasn't doing so good on the road and everybody wanted to get back to Pensacola, you…
